issue.title: Implement a TodoMVC application
issue.body:
Context:

This repository is empty. We want the agentic SDLC pipeline to start with a Spec Agent contract for implementing the canonical TodoMVC app. The implementation will come later; this issue is only asking the Spec Agent to produce a clear implementation contract and acceptance-test plan.

Reference material:

Use the official TodoMVC application specification as the product source of truth:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tastejs/todomvc/refs/heads/master/app-spec.md

Concrete target:

Create a TodoMVC web app implementation spec for a React app. The app should be browser-runnable from a normal project entry point, with an `index.html` document that mounts React into `#root`, and React source files under `src/`. Use a lightweight Vite-style project shape unless the project context provides a different React convention.

Base project shape:

- `index.html` contains the `#root` mount element and loads the React entry module.
- `src/main.jsx` mounts React.
- `src/App.jsx` owns the TodoMVC behavior.
- `src/styles.css` or equivalent CSS provides TodoMVC presentation.
- The implementation may add small internal modules under `src/` when useful, but must remain a browser-runnable React single page app.

Testing baseline:

- Use Playwright end-to-end tests as the expected executable test strategy.
- Put tests under `tests/` and use the project Playwright configuration when present.
- Tests should interact with public TodoMVC UI controls and standard TodoMVC class names, not private implementation functions.
- Tests should navigate through the configured base URL or `/`, not hardcoded local filesystem paths.
- Tests should cover behavior, persistence, routing, and edge cases from the acceptance criteria.

Expected local tooling context:

- `python3` may be used for simple static serving when the project config requires it.
- `node`, `npm`, and `npx` are expected to be available for project-defined JavaScript commands.
- The base project manifest should declare React, ReactDOM, Vite, the Vite React plugin, and Playwright before agents run.
- `git` is expected to be available for repository inspection when needed.
- Node package-manager commands may be used when project manifests require them.
- The Test Agent may install dependencies and may add test-only tooling dependencies when the approved test strategy requires them.
- The Test Agent may run generated tests to prove the suite is red before implementation, but must not fix production code.
- The Test Agent must report every dependency manifest or lockfile change in its output contract.
- The Test Agent must not add production implementation dependencies unless the approved spec or project context explicitly defines them as part of the test target.

Required behavior to cover:

- When there are no todos, the main todo list area and footer are hidden.
- The new-todo input is focused on page load.
- Pressing Enter in the new-todo input creates a todo only after trimming whitespace and rejecting empty input.
- The new-todo input is cleared after a todo is created.
- The mark-all checkbox toggles all todos and reflects whether all individual todos are complete.
- Each todo can be marked complete or active individually.
- Double-clicking a todo label enters editing mode and focuses the edit input.
- Edits are saved on blur and Enter after trimming whitespace.
- Empty edited titles destroy the todo.
- Escape while editing discards changes and exits editing mode.
- Hovering a todo shows its remove button.
- The active counter is pluralized correctly: 0 items, 1 item, 2 items.
- The clear-completed button is visible only when completed todos exist and removes completed todos when clicked.
- Todos persist to localStorage using item fields compatible with id, title, and completed.
- Editing state is not persisted.
- Routes are supported for all, active, and completed filters using #/, #/active, and #/completed.
- Changing routes filters the todo list and updates the selected filter link.
- If a todo changes state while filtered, the visible list updates immediately.
- The active route/filter persists across reloads.

Non-goals for this first spec:

- Do not implement the app.
- Do not generate production code.
- Do not generate executable tests yet.
- Do not add dependencies unrelated to the approved React implementation.
- Do not change or reinterpret TodoMVC behavior beyond the official spec.

Known ambiguity:

- Browser support policy is not defined in this repo yet.
- The exact React component boundaries are not chosen beyond following the project context and a minimal Vite-style shape.

Spec Agent instruction:

Create a specification contract only. The output must include acceptance criteria, affected components/artifacts, edge cases, non-goals, risks, cost plan, model routing recommendation, and an implementation test plan. Ask only blocking questions.
